Management Plan

- Advised urgent face-to-face assessment at GP hub today for physical examination and possible blood work.  
- Warned of potential need for hospital referral to rule out meningitis, dengue, or other travel-related infections.  
- Educated on red-flag symptoms (worsening rash, non-blanching rash, photophobia, neck stiffness, vomiting) and instructed to attend emergency department if unable to obtain prompt GP review.  
- No prescriptions issued during telehealth consult.

Consider:
- Possible infectious diseases referral following examination and initial labs.  
- CTG registration, preventive health checks, and immunisation review at follow-up (not yet addressed).

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, temperature, full systems review, immunisation status, smoking/alcohol history, mental health screening, BMI, urinalysis.  
● Internal contradictions: Patient initially answered “Yep” to difficulty looking at light, then immediately stated light “doesn’t seem to bother me.” (conflict noted re photophobia).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor overlaps and incomplete sentences but sufficient to extract key clinical data.
